name: Indonesia
genZNote: Indonesia is so spread out across 17,000+ islands that it spans three time zones — it's basically proof that a country can be an archipelago the size of a continent and still hold together as the world's third-largest democracy.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The world's largest archipelagic country, made up of over 17,000 islands spanning Southeast Asia, including Java, Sumatra, Borneo (Kalimantan), Sulawesi, and part of New Guinea (Papua).
Sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, giving it one of the highest concentrations of active volcanoes in the world and frequent seismic activity.
Home to some of the world's most biodiverse tropical rainforests, though facing significant deforestation pressure.
Building a new capital city, Nusantara, on Borneo, intended to replace the sinking, congested Jakarta.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: The world's most populous Muslim-majority country, though officially a secular state recognising six religions and hundreds of ethnic groups and languages.
Bahasa Indonesia is the unifying national language; the national motto 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika' ('Unity in Diversity') reflects its extraordinary ethnic and linguistic diversity.
Rich traditional arts include Javanese and Balinese gamelan music, batik textiles (a UNESCO-recognised craft), and wayang shadow puppetry.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic and the world's third-largest democracy by population, with a directly elected President and a bicameral legislature.
Adheres to 'Pancasila', its official state ideology of five principles including belief in one God, humanitarianism, unity, democracy, and social justice.
Highly decentralised administratively, with power devolved to provinces following the fall of the Suharto regime in 1998.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Home to major biodiversity research given its rainforest and marine ecosystems, contributing to global conservation science.
Growing pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing base, including state-owned Bio Farma, a significant regional vaccine producer.
Prone to major natural disasters (earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions), driving strong national expertise in disaster-response science.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G20 member and the largest economy in Southeast Asia; founding member and de facto leader of ASEAN.
Pursues a long-standing foreign policy of non-alignment, dating back to hosting the 1955 Bandung Conference of newly independent Asian and African nations.
Plays an active role in international Islamic diplomacy as the world's most populous Muslim-majority nation.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Indonesia share a 'Comprehensive Strategic Partnership' and centuries-old cultural and religious links through the historic spread of Hinduism and Buddhism across the archipelago.
Bali retains a Hindu-majority population and temple culture directly descended from ancient Indian religious influence, a point of deep cultural connection.
Growing defence cooperation and trade ties, with India importing coal and palm oil, and both countries collaborating within the G20 and Indo-Pacific frameworks.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Southeast Asia's largest economy, driven by natural resources (coal, palm oil, nickel), manufacturing, and a large domestic consumer market.
The world's largest producer and exporter of palm oil, and a major global nickel producer, crucial for electric-vehicle battery supply chains.
A founding ASEAN member benefiting from regional trade integration and growing foreign investment in manufacturing.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the world's largest archipelago and most populous Muslim-majority country.
Bali's unique Hindu culture and world-famous beaches and temples.
Leading global producer of palm oil and nickel.
Ancient Buddhist and Hindu monuments such as Borobudur and Prambanan.
Being a founding member and leading voice of ASEAN.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic nation and most populous Muslim-majority country, governed as a presidential republic and leading ASEAN member.
keyFacts: Capital: moving from Jakarta to Nusantara (Borneo). Currency: Indonesian Rupiah.
Official state ideology: Pancasila (five founding principles).
World's largest palm oil producer and a major nickel exporter.
Founding member of ASEAN; host of the 1955 Bandung Conference.
commonConfusion: Indonesia is a secular state with a Muslim-majority population, not an Islamic state — Pancasila recognises multiple religions.

highYieldFacts: Indonesia: presidential republic, world's largest archipelago, capital relocating to Nusantara.
Founding ASEAN member; hosted the 1955 Bandung Conference of Non-Aligned nations.
World's largest palm oil producer; major nickel exporter (key for EV batteries).
commonTraps: Assuming Indonesia is officially an Islamic state — it is constitutionally pluralist under Pancasila.
Confusing Bali's Hindu-majority culture with the country's overall Muslim-majority demographic.
mustRemember: Indonesia: ASEAN leader, world's biggest archipelago, palm oil/nickel giant, deep historic Hindu-Buddhist links with India via Bali and ancient temples.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Indonesia Relations
